intro: Connect a data source, then go AI designs → review & refine → save. Once saved it appears in your datasets. Structure analysis runs automatically in the background, so press "View structure" only when you want to check it.

restore.note: Restored your previous work (re-select the source only if you need to re-run).
restore.clearConfirm: This clears everything in progress, including the AI-proposed design and save results. Continue?

redesign.banner: Revising the design of the existing dataset {{name}}. Saving updates this same dataset's mapping (apply the data via "Update data (re-ingest)").
redesign.bannerAdopted: This design is saved as the dataset {{name}}. Further saves (redo / re-save after an AI fix) update this same dataset — no new dataset is created.
redesign.findingsBody: The same points are already in the review comment box below — press “Apply comment & regenerate” to have the AI fix them. If you only want to adjust item meanings, you can dismiss this.

step.guard: Generate a schema first in "AI designs".

source.label: Data source
source.note: Any structured source planned (currently CSV/TSV/instrument text (.txt/.dat/.asc) / JSON / documents)
source.footSelected: {{n}} file(s) selected — the same source is used in every step
source.footEmpty: The source you choose here is shared across every step

design.hint: The AI proposes a draft of the data's blueprint (vocabulary) and ingestion rules. It uses the model selected in Settings.
design.hintsLegend: Hints (optional — checking the ones that apply improves accuracy)
design.domainFreePlaceholder: e.g. In this field A and B are two names for the same quantity. Figure values were read with WebPlotDigitizer.
design.inspectDetails: Show the structure analysis this proposal used

review.hint: Review the proposal; comment on what you want changed and the AI regenerates it (optional).
review.commentPlaceholder: e.g. Make the Sample IRI a composite key of (SID, sample_id). Update the design rationale to match.

save.hint: Splits the design into 4 artifacts and runs 8 automatic checks before saving to your datasets.
save.duplicateNote: Already saved, so the save button is disabled. Redoing via "Save again" below updates this same dataset — it never creates another one.
save.incompleteHeading: The design was saved, but it can't be ingested as-is
save.noRml: No conversion rule (RML) was generated, so this data can't be ingested. Redesign it, or fill it in via "Review & refine".
save.incomplete: The design is incomplete, so it can't be ingested as-is. Redesign it, or fill it in via "Review & refine".
save.validationHead: Validating the design against the source data found these problems (fix them here before ingest):
save.backToKantan: Back to simple mode and continue
save.advisoryHead: Weak spots in this design (you can still save)

fix.hint: The validation above reported failures and/or warnings. In one click, hand those specifics to the AI to rebuild the design (including §RML). After it regenerates, press "Confirm & save" again to re-validate.
fix.needKey: To let the AI fix this, set up a model and key in Settings.
fix.commentIntro: Fix the following validation errors and rebuild §RML (use only the allowed Tier 0 functions; do not reference columns that don't exist):

autocorrect.converged: The AI auto-validated the design (resolved every issue in {{rounds}} self-correction round(s))
autocorrect.bestEffort: The AI self-corrected {{rounds}} round(s) but {{count}} issue(s) remain
autocorrect.cleanFirst: The AI's first design had no static issues
autocorrect.prefillFix: Copied the remaining issues into the fix box below — use “Ask AI to fix” to retry.
autocorrect.caveat: This is a static check against the real data; convergence does NOT guarantee it will ingest (the ingest gate re-checks).
autocorrect.tabularCaveat: References into JSON/XML sources were NOT column-checked.
autocorrect.coverageCaveat: The self-correction may have reduced how much of the source is mapped — review the design's coverage.

job.elapsed: {{mm}}m {{ss}}s elapsed · usually 1–6 min · connection is kept alive
job.elapsedStatus: {{mm}}m {{ss}}s elapsed · usually 1–6 min · connection is kept alive · status: {{status}}
job.resumedFailed: Could not resume the interrupted job: {{message}}

materialize.summaryOk: No blocking issues — OK to save
materialize.summaryBad: Blocking issues found (code {{code}}) — fix before saving

trap.T1: IRI uniqueness (is the composite key globally unique?)
trap.T2: BOM (is the source read as utf-8-sig?)
trap.T5: Mermaid colon avoidance (no : in diagram labels)

ingest.heading: Import data (human gate)
ingest.noRml: This design has no ingestion rules (RML), so it cannot be ingested. Once the "AI designs" step emits them, you can safely ingest from here.
ingest.note: When you approve, Morph-KGC runs this declarative RML (no generated code runs — only the verified Tier 0 functions) and ingests the result into an isolated draft graph. It does not touch Ask's default citation surface (canonical).
ingest.doneCount: ✓ Ingested into the draft graph ({{n}} triples).
ingest.notSaved: This design has not been saved yet (no dataset found).
ingest.needCsv: Ingestion needs the source file (CSV/TSV/instrument text) used in the design. Re-select it in the data source panel (re-selection is required after a reload).
ingest.cancelled: Ingest cancelled. Any partially written data has been discarded.

hints.compositeKey: The same ID may appear in other files/papers (a combination may be needed to tell rows apart)
hints.prov: Always record where each value came from (paper / experiment / ingest run)
hints.noBnode: (Technical option) avoid unnamed intermediate nodes — makes re-ingest robust
hints.units: Unify unit and quantity spellings (e.g. S/cm vs S·cm⁻¹)
hints.jsonColumns: Some columns contain JSON (arrays or objects) inside cells

skeleton.discardConfirm: This discards the generated skeleton and your edits. Continue?

rethink.label: If the AI read it wrong, tell it here and have it think again
rethink.placeholder: e.g. One row is one measurement of one sample — split samples and measurements into separate kinds
rethink.needsFiles: Re-attach the files to ask the AI again (unavailable while the sources are gone).

diagram.note: Boxes = kinds of data (what one row becomes). Lines = ID links (inferred from how IDs are built).

skeleton.confirmCollides: In "{{maps}}", several rows still get an overlapping ID. If you continue, rows that overlap merge into one. Proceed?
skeleton.gateHint: Check the AI's proposal of which table holds what kind of data, and how each row gets its ID. Column meanings (properties) are generated after this. The evidence under each row shows, from your data, whether every row gets its own ID.
skeleton.colKey: How each row gets its ID
skeleton.colClassesPlain: What one record is (kind of data)

evidence.unique: All {{rows}} rows get their own ID
evidence.collides: {{colliding}} of {{total}} rows get an ID that overlaps another row (rows that overlap merge into one)
evidence.collisionExample: e.g. lines {{lines}}: {{count}} rows share one ID ({{values}})
evidence.singleton: All {{total}} rows merge into one record (file-wide information)
evidence.cardMerges: {{rows}} rows of information gather onto this one card
evidence.cardMore: …and {{count}} more cards of the same shape
evidence.cardConflict: Rows disagree — this one record ends up carrying BOTH values
evidence.cardBorrowedBand: Below: values “{{map}}” owns — the same content copies onto all {{count}} records here
evidence.cardDelegatedBand: Below: “{{map}}” territory — not on this card
evidence.cardDelegatedBandPlain: Below: values that change per row — not on this card
evidence.cardBorrowedWhy: This value does not change per record, so keeping it here would copy the same content onto every row. It is stored once on “{{map}}” and read from here by following the link.
evidence.gapHead: {{columns}} will not be imported as things stand (no per-row kind holds them yet)
evidence.gapAdd: Create the per-row kind ({{count}} records, ID built from {{key}})
evidence.growthHead: Is another THING mixed in here? (pick columns to split into their own kind)
evidence.growthPerFile: This card is one per file ({{count}} so far).
evidence.growthDescribed: {{count}} column(s) get recorded separately per file.
evidence.growthSharedHead: {{count}} columns hold the same value as another file — split them into a kind and they fold into one record
evidence.riskMeasurementId: This ID is built only from measured values ({{columns}}). If a value is ever corrected, a new ID appears and citations of the old one lose their target.
evidence.riskScopeMissing: This ID has no column telling one “{{parent}}” from another ({{columns}}). Nothing overlaps within this file, but appended data from another {{parent}} could merge into the same ID.
evidence.appliedKeyFix: The AI chose “{{from}}” for the ID, but an ID built only from measured values loses its citations when the value is ever corrected. The machine replaced it with “{{to}}”.
evidence.appliedKeyFixRevert: Go back to the AI's choice
evidence.candidatesSingletonHead: Should this actually be one record per row? (click a column set to apply)
evidence.scopedCandidate: Safe under future appends — never merges with another card's rows
evidence.candidatesHead: Column combinations where every row is distinct (click to apply)
evidence.measurementOnly: A measurement column — it may be unique only by accident; not recommended as an ID
evidence.measurementKeyCaution: This ID is built from measured values. Every row is unique in today's data, but adding data may cause overlaps. Combining it with a column whose values never change — a sample name or a serial number — is safer (pick one from the candidates below)
evidence.classNumericKeyCaution: The type name “{{cls}}” looks like a measured column ({{column}}). Naming the type after what one ROW is (e.g. a measurement point) is safer
evidence.undeclaredPrefixes: Undeclared prefixes: {{prefixes}} (saving will fail until they are declared)
evidence.undeclaredPrefixesPlain: The AI's ID recipe has a part that cannot be fixed on this screen. Press “Have the AI think again” below.
evidence.missingColumns: The AI used columns that are not in the file ({{columns}}) to build the ID. Pick again from the candidates below, or fix the ID recipe yourself.
evidence.missingColumnsPlain: The AI used columns that are not in the file ({{columns}}) to build the ID. Pick again from the candidates below, or have the AI think again.
evidence.missingColumnSuggestion: The column “{{wrong}}” the AI named is not in this table. Closest match: “{{suggestion}}” (tap to fix).
evidence.constant: This kind gets ONE ID per file (document) — there are no per-row checks
evidence.unsupported: Automatic checking for this source type is not supported yet (validated after generation)
evidence.sourceNotFound: Could not check: the file was not found. This ID's uniqueness and safety are unverified (drop the file again to check)
evidence.sourceNotFoundNamed: Could not check: the file the design reads, “{{name}}”, was not found. This ID's uniqueness and safety are unverified (drop “{{name}}” again to check)
evidence.noTemplate: The AI did not settle on how to build IDs for this kind. Pick from the candidates below, or write the ID recipe yourself.
evidence.noTemplatePlain: The AI did not settle on how to build IDs for this kind. Pick from the candidates below, or have the AI think again.
evidence.notChecked: This kind could not be checked. Its ID's uniqueness and safety are unverified (drop the file again to check it)
evidence.notCheckedNamed: Could not check the file the design reads, “{{name}}”. This ID's uniqueness and safety are unverified (drop “{{name}}” again to check it)
evidence.reattach: Re-attach the file to re-check edited IDs
evidence.sourceMismatch: The file you put, “{{present}}”, doesn't match the name the design reads, “{{name}}”
evidence.gapNeedsFiles: Re-attach the files to create this kind (the check runs there too).
evidence.splitLead: If some of these columns name one shared thing, split just those into their own kind. Then another file carrying the same values lands on the same one record.
evidence.splitAdd: Split the {{count}} checked column(s) into their own kind
evidence.candidatesQuietHead: Build the ID from a different set of columns? (click a column set to apply)
evidence.splitPick: Make this column its own kind: {{column}}
evidence.catalogMerges: Rows with the same value merge: {{rows}} rows → {{count}} records (intended — this is a value kind)

ns.title: Namespaces (where this design mints its IDs)
ns.hint: Classes and data IDs are minted under these namespaces and become permanent identifiers. Reused standard vocabularies (schema: etc.) stay as they are — check that the design's own namespaces live where you intend.
ns.hintPlain: Addresses the AI wrote for the IDs. You normally do not need to touch these.
ns.placeholderWarn: This is a placeholder domain (example.org etc.) — it can never become a citable identifier. Edit the namespace.
ns.placeholderWarnPlain: Still a placeholder address (example.org etc.) — it cannot become a citable ID. Have the AI think again, or fix it in Detail mode.
ns.confirmPlaceholder: Some namespaces still point at a placeholder domain ({{prefixes}}). Continue anyway? (The self-correction pass will try to re-mint, but fixing it here is the sure path.)
ns.nameLabel: The name inside the permanent ID (the display name is given separately at “Publish”)
ns.nameHint: The name inside the ID (letters, digits and hyphens only). The display name shown in the catalog is given separately at the last step, “Publish”. Pick a name that still fits data you will add later (e.g. the kind of measurement rather than one material).
ns.baseUnconfigured: The ID issuer is still a provisional address ({{base}}). That is fine for trying things out. To keep IDs citable after publishing, set the issuer address under Settings → “This server” (on a shared server, this is set once for everyone).
ns.advancedNote: Shorthands (al3v: etc.) are display abbreviations — changing them never changes the data. They are re-derived automatically when you rename the dataset. You can also edit the namespace URLs directly here.

dialect.title: Read settings (optional)
dialect.hint: The read format (encoding, delimiter, lines before the header) was auto-detected. Correct it here before generating if it is wrong. Clean CSVs are not shown.

preamble.keyvalue_cells: Delimited key=value cells → columns (instrument meta line)
preamble.hint: Ingest the preamble metadata as columns broadcast onto every data row (so a sample name, a measurement date, etc. can be queried alongside the measurements).
